aiMessages.content:
Create a WhatsApp Business bot only. Do not create a Telegram bot. Do not deploy this bot to Telegram. This bot is intended only for WhatsApp private chats using WhatsApp Business or WhatsApp Business API.

The bot is the official WhatsApp assistant for:

University: Federal University Wukari
Faculty: Faculty of Computing and Information Systems
Department: Department of Software Engineering

The bot should introduce itself as:
“Hello, I am the official WhatsApp assistant for the Department of Software Engineering, Faculty of Computing and Information Systems, Federal University Wukari. I can help you with department announcements, lecturer information, courses, timetables, fees, deadlines, venues, and other approved department information.”

This must be a WhatsApp bot, not a Telegram bot. All interaction examples, user flows, and deployment assumptions should be based on WhatsApp private chat. Do not use Telegram-specific features such as Telegram usernames, Telegram groups, Telegram commands, inline keyboards, Telegram bot tokens, or Telegram channel setup.

The bot should help students get accurate department information through WhatsApp private chat. Students should be able to message the department WhatsApp bot directly and ask questions naturally.

All data should be stored and managed using Google Sheets.

Create or connect the following Google Sheets tables:

1) Announcements
Fields:
AnnouncementID, Title, Category, Level, CourseCode, Message, DatePosted, ExpiryDate, Priority, Status

2) Lecturers
Fields:
LecturerID, FullName, Title, DepartmentRole, OfficeLocation, PhoneNumber, Email, CoursesTaught, OfficeHours, Bio, PhotoURL, Status

3) Courses
Fields:
CourseCode, CourseTitle, Level, Semester, LecturerName, Venue, Schedule, Description, Status

4) Timetable
Fields:
Level, CourseCode, CourseTitle, Day, Time, Venue, LecturerName, Status

5) DepartmentInfo
Fields:
InfoType, Title, Details, ContactPerson, ContactPhone, LastUpdated, Status

The bot should support two types of users:

1) Admins
Admins are approved department staff or representatives.
Admins should be verified by their WhatsApp phone number or by an admin access code.
Admins can add, edit, remove, and view information stored in Google Sheets.
Admins can manage announcements, lecturer details, courses, timetables, and general department information.

Admin actions should be done using normal WhatsApp messages such as:
“Add announcement”
“Update announcement”
“Delete announcement”
“View active announcements”
“Add lecturer”
“Update lecturer”
“Add course”
“Update timetable”

Do not use Telegram-style slash commands.

2) Students
Students can ask questions naturally in WhatsApp private chat.

Examples of student questions:
“What is the latest announcement?”
“Show me 300 level announcements”
“When is the CSC 302 test?”
“What is today’s lecture update?”
“Who teaches CSC 302?”
“Show me Dr. Musa’s details”
“What courses does Dr. Amina teach?”
“Where is Mr. John’s office?”
“Send Dr. Bello’s picture”
“What is the department fee?”
“Show me the timetable for 200 level”
“Who is the department contact person?”
The bot should search the Google Sheets data and reply with the most relevant confirmed information.

For lecturer questions, the bot should be able to return:
Lecturer name
Title
Department role
Office location
Phone number
Email
Courses taught
Office hours
Short bio
Lecturer photo, using the PhotoURL field

If the WhatsApp integration supports sending images, the bot should send the lecturer’s photo directly. If image sending is not supported, the bot should send the photo link from the PhotoURL field.

The bot must not invent information. If the information is not found in Google Sheets, it should reply:
“I don’t have confirmed information on that yet. Please check back later or contact the Department of Software Engineering representative.”

The bot should prioritize active and current records only. Expired announcements should not be shown unless an admin asks for them.

The bot should keep responses clear, short, and suitable for WhatsApp chat.

The bot should respect privacy and only share lecturer details that are already approved by the department for student access.

Important deployment instruction:
Deploy this assistant as a WhatsApp Business bot only. If WhatsApp setup is not connected, ask me to connect WhatsApp Business or WhatsApp Business API first. Do not create a Telegram bot as a fallback.

planMarkdown:
Bot: Wukari SE Desk

Summary:
A WhatsApp-only private chat assistant for the Department of Software Engineering, Faculty of Computing and Information Systems, Federal University Wukari. It uses CookMyBots for managed WhatsApp transport and Google Sheets as the department-managed information source for announcements, lecturers, courses, timetables, and general department information.

Product goals:
Provide students with fast, accurate, approved department information through WhatsApp private chat only. The bot must introduce itself as: “Hello, I am the official WhatsApp assistant for the Department of Software Engineering, Faculty of Computing and Information Systems, Federal University Wukari. I can help you with department announcements, lecturer information, courses, timetables, fees, deadlines, venues, and other approved department information.” It must answer natural student questions, support staff/admin updates through normal WhatsApp messages, keep replies short and clear, and never invent information. If confirmed data is unavailable, it must reply: “I don’t have confirmed information on that yet. Please check back later or contact the Department of Software Engineering representative.”

High-level architecture:
Single Node.js ESM service connected to CookMyBots managed WhatsApp transport for receiving and sending WhatsApp private chat messages. No Telegram support, no Telegram fallback, no Telegram tokens, no Telegram commands, and no Telegram deployment path. The service contains: 1) WhatsApp message adapter for CookMyBots inbound/outbound messages, 2) intent router for student questions and admin actions, 3) Google Sheets repository layer for all department data, 4) admin verification module using approved WhatsApp phone numbers and/or access codes, 5) response formatter optimized for WhatsApp chat, 6) optional media sender for lecturer photos when image sending is supported by the WhatsApp transport. If WhatsApp Business or WhatsApp Business API is not connected in CookMyBots, the bot should ask the owner to connect WhatsApp first and should not create another platform bot. The service should treat Google Sheets as the source of truth and should refresh/read data from Sheets on demand or with a short cache window to avoid stale answers.

Data model:
Primary data store: Google Sheets. Required sheets: Announcements with fields AnnouncementID, Title, Category, Level, CourseCode, Message, DatePosted, ExpiryDate, Priority, Status. Lecturers with fields LecturerID, FullName, Title, DepartmentRole, OfficeLocation, PhoneNumber, Email, CoursesTaught, OfficeHours, Bio, PhotoURL, Status. Courses with fields CourseCode, CourseTitle, Level, Semester, LecturerName, Venue, Schedule, Description, Status. Timetable with fields Level, CourseCode, CourseTitle, Day, Time, Venue, LecturerName, Status. DepartmentInfo with fields InfoType, Title, Details, ContactPerson, ContactPhone, LastUpdated, Status. Recommended additional Google Sheets for operations: AdminUsers with fields PhoneNumber, FullName, Role, AccessCodeHash, Status, LastVerifiedAt; AuditLog with fields Timestamp, AdminPhone, Action, SheetName, RecordID, BeforeValue, AfterValue, Result. Status should be used consistently, for example Active, Inactive, Draft, Archived. Announcements should be shown to students only when Status is Active and ExpiryDate is empty or in the future. Expired announcements remain available only to verified admins.

Key flows:
Student onboarding: when a student first messages the WhatsApp number, the bot sends the official introduction and examples of what they can ask. Student question flow: normalize the message, detect intent such as announcement, timetable, course, lecturer, fee, deadline, venue, contact, or general information, search active/current Google Sheets rows, rank exact matches first by course code, level, lecturer name, date, and priority, then reply with the most relevant confirmed information. Lecturer photo flow: when a student asks for a lecturer picture, find the active lecturer row and use PhotoURL; if CookMyBots image sending is available, send the image, otherwise send the link. Admin verification flow: an admin is verified automatically if their WhatsApp phone number is approved, or manually by sending an admin access code. Admin management flow: verified admins send normal WhatsApp phrases such as Add announcement, Update lecturer, or Update timetable; the bot asks step-by-step for required fields, validates the data, writes to Google Sheets, confirms the change, and records an audit entry. Delete flow should preferably mark records Inactive or Archived instead of physically deleting rows, unless the department explicitly allows hard deletion. Unknown or missing information flow: never guess; send the approved fallback message. Privacy flow: only share lecturer contact details that are present in active approved Google Sheets records.

Tech stack:
Runtime: single Node.js service using ESM. WhatsApp transport: CookMyBots managed WhatsApp integration for private chat inbound and outbound messages. Data management: Google Sheets API as the source of truth for all department content. Optional persistence: MongoDB only if needed for non-authoritative conversation state, short-lived admin workflows, idempotency, or audit backup; department content remains in Google Sheets. Media: lecturer photos referenced by PhotoURL and delivered through WhatsApp media support when available, otherwise returned as links. Configuration: environment variables for Google credentials, spreadsheet IDs, CookMyBots connection settings, cache settings, and bot identity. Do not require WhatsApp Cloud API webhook implementation or WHATSAPPTOKEN, WHATSAPPPHONENUMBERID, or WHATSAPPVERIFYTOKEN.

Non-functional requirements:
Accuracy is mandatory: the bot must only answer from approved Google Sheets records. Availability should be suitable for department daily use, with graceful handling of Google Sheets API delays or failures. Security: protect Google credentials, restrict admin actions by phone number/access code, validate all admin inputs, and keep audit logs. Privacy: expose only department-approved lecturer details. Reliability: handle duplicate inbound messages idempotently where possible and avoid partial writes during admin workflows. Performance: cache sheet reads briefly but invalidate or refresh after admin updates. Maintainability: keep sheets, repository methods, intent handlers, and response templates separated. Deployment: deploy as a single service process with WhatsApp connected through CookMyBots only; if WhatsApp is not connected, prompt to connect WhatsApp Business or WhatsApp Business API first and do not deploy to Telegram or any fallback chat platform.

Bot commands:
• Latest announcement — Shows the most recent active department announcements. (usage: latest announcement) [student]
• Level announcements — Shows active announcements for a specific student level. (usage: show me 300 level announcements) [student]
• Course lecturer — Finds who teaches a specific course. (usage: who teaches CSC 302?) [student]
• Lecturer details — Returns approved details for a lecturer, including role, office, contact, courses, office hours, and bio where available. (usage: show me Dr. Musa's details) [student]
• Lecturer photo — Sends the lecturer photo from the approved PhotoURL field or returns the photo link if direct image sending is unavailable. (usage: send Dr. Bello's picture) [student]
• Level timetable — Shows the active timetable for a specified level. (usage: show me the timetable for 200 level) [student]
• Department fee — Returns active approved fee information from DepartmentInfo. (usage: what is the department fee?) [student]
• Department contact — Returns the approved department contact person and phone number. (usage: who is the department contact person?) [student]
• Add announcement — Starts an admin workflow to create a new announcement in Google Sheets. (usage: Add announcement) [admin]
• Update announcement — Starts an admin workflow to edit an existing announcement. (usage: Update announcement) [admin]
• Delete announcement — Allows a verified admin to archive or deactivate an announcement. (usage: Delete announcement) [admin]
• View active announcements — Shows active announcements to a verified admin, including IDs for editing. (usage: View active announcements) [admin]
• Add lecturer — Starts an admin workflow to add lecturer information. (usage: Add lecturer) [admin]
• Update lecturer — Starts an admin workflow to update lecturer information. (usage: Update lecturer) [admin]
• Add course — Starts an admin workflow to add a course record. (usage: Add course) [admin]
• Update timetable — Starts an admin workflow to add or edit timetable entries. (usage: Update timetable) [admin]

envVarDocs.title: CookMyBots WhatsApp Webhook Secret
envVarDocs.description: Verifies inbound managed WhatsApp webhook requests from CookMyBots.
envVarDocs.howToGet: Injected or configured by CookMyBots for the deployed bot.

envVarDocs.title: CookMyBots AI Endpoint
envVarDocs.description: Base URL for the CookMyBots AI Gateway.
envVarDocs.usage: The bot appends /chat for intent classification.

envVarDocs.title: AI Timeout
envVarDocs.description: Maximum AI Gateway request time in milliseconds.

envVarDocs.title: AI Max Retries
envVarDocs.description: Number of AI Gateway retry attempts.

envVarDocs.title: Concurrency
envVarDocs.description: Runtime concurrency setting used with conservative AI backpressure.
envVarDocs.usage: Defaults to 20, with AI in-flight capped internally.

envVarDocs.title: Web3 Chat Mode
envVarDocs.description: AI Gateway routing mode. This bot defaults to off because it is a university department assistant.

envVarDocs.title: Google Sheets Spreadsheet ID
envVarDocs.description: Spreadsheet used as the source of truth for department data.
envVarDocs.usage: Used by the Google Sheets repository for all reads and writes.
envVarDocs.howToGet: Copy from the Google Sheet URL.

envVarDocs.title: Google Service Account Email
envVarDocs.description: Service account email with edit access to the spreadsheet.
envVarDocs.usage: Used for Google Sheets API authentication.
envVarDocs.howToGet: Create a Google Cloud service account and share the sheet with this email.

envVarDocs.title: Google Private Key
envVarDocs.description: Private key for the Google service account.
envVarDocs.usage: Used for Google Sheets API authentication.
envVarDocs.howToGet: Download the service account JSON key and copy the private_key value.

envVarDocs.title: Google Private Key Base64
envVarDocs.usage: Preferred if the hosting provider has trouble with multiline private keys.
envVarDocs.howToGet: Base64 encode the private_key value from the service account JSON.

envVarDocs.title: Google Sheets Cache TTL
envVarDocs.description: Short read cache duration for Google Sheets reads.

envVarDocs.title: Admin Phone Numbers
envVarDocs.description: Optional comma-separated approved WhatsApp admin phone numbers.
envVarDocs.usage: Auto-verifies admins by sender phone number.
envVarDocs.howToGet: Set manually using approved department staff numbers.

envVarDocs.title: Admin Access Code Hash

envVarDocs.usage: Verifies admins who send admin code YOUR_CODE.
envVarDocs.howToGet: Hash the approved code with SHA-256.

envVarDocs.title: Admin Access Code
envVarDocs.description: Optional plain admin access code for quick setup.
envVarDocs.usage: Verifies admins who send admin code YOUR_CODE.
envVarDocs.howToGet: Set manually. Prefer ADMIN_ACCESS_CODE_HASH in production.

envVarDocs.title: MongoDB URI
envVarDocs.description: Optional storage for conversation traces and admin workflow state.
envVarDocs.usage: The bot remains functional with in-memory state if missing, but MongoDB is recommended for production.
envVarDocs.howToGet: Create a MongoDB database and copy the connection URI.
